title: Top-down PLM assembly with trainable temporal dynamics and bottom-up adaptive-state ablation
question: Does allowing three persistent temporal decay constants to adapt end-to-end on training histories improve held-out temporal-filter transfer over the matched fixed three-timescale state?
hypothesis: The null from broader fixed temporal coverage indicates that raw state-bank width is not the primary bottleneck; learning the temporal decay constants from training histories should improve transfer if fixed scale placement is the limiting mechanism.

endpoints.name: heldout_temporal_success
endpoints.description: Exact class-balanced success on a new held-out temporal-filter set disjoint from every filter constant used in training and from prior transfer-lane test constants; primary decision at H=256.

endpoints.name: history_conditioned_action_gap
endpoints.description: Fraction of exact negation pairs for which the policy selects opposite actions despite identical current observation.

endpoints.name: learned_decay_constants
endpoints.description: Final three adaptive decay constants after training; descriptive only.

endpoints.name: state_intervention
endpoints.description: Frozen adaptive-checkpoint success after zeroing or cross-episode shuffling persistent state.

endpoints.name: computation_work
endpoints.description: Explicit evaluation work including persistent-state update, policy computation, executor and verifier.

decision_rule.condition: At H=256, three_adaptive exceeds three_fixed in heldout_temporal_success by more than 0.10, the registered seed-bootstrap 95% confidence interval for the paired seed-level difference excludes zero, and three_adaptive exceeds no_state.
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence that trainable temporal decay parameters improve held-out temporal-filter transfer under the registered persistent-state loop and matched policy parameter count.
decision_rule.does_not_license: global temporal optimality, power-law or scale-free memory, biological equivalence, natural multimodal competence, asymptotic scaling, or hardware speedup.

decision_rule.condition: three_adaptive does not beat three_fixed materially, but both stateful arms retain a history-conditioned action gap and outperform no_state.
decision_rule.licenses: persistent temporal state is useful but trainable decay placement is not established as a sufficient improvement on this transfer benchmark.
decision_rule.does_not_license: failure of adaptive temporal memory generally or optimality of the fixed scales.

decision_rule.condition: three_adaptive loses to no_state or cannot preserve a history-conditioned action gap.
decision_rule.licenses: the registered adaptive temporal-memory mechanism is not established on this benchmark.

held_constant: adaptive-lane test temporal-filter alphas are exactly 0.41,0.57,0.76,0.875,0.925,0.991,0.994
the adaptive-lane test set is disjoint from training constants and from prior transfer-lane test constants
current observation at decision is exactly 0.0
paired histories are exact negations with opposite gold actions
policy parameter count is exactly 86 for every registered arm
policy learning rate is exactly 0.05 and decay learning rate is exactly 0.02
optimizer family, training steps, evaluation sample count, executor, verifier, state-update recurrence, and work-accounting definition
no test temporal-filter constant is used for training, decay initialization, checkpoint selection, or hyperparameter selection
